headline: Apple and Micron clash before Trump over Chinese memory chips, report says
summary: A Wall Street Journal report indicates Micron is lobbying the Trump administration to block Apple's efforts to source memory chips from Chinese suppliers.
details: According to The Wall Street Journal, Micron Technology is actively pressing the Trump administration to intervene and prevent Apple from using memory chips manufactured by Chinese suppliers. This reported move underscores increasing friction within the global technology supply chain.

The dispute highlights the complexities of international trade relations and the strategic importance of semiconductor manufacturing. Both companies are major players in the tech industry, with significant stakes in global markets.

headline_marked: [[Real-Time AI Voice Agent Handles 70+ Languages]] for businesses, built with model-agnostic approach
headline: Real-Time AI Voice Agent Handles 70+ Languages for businesses, built with model-agnostic approach
summary: RingBot is an Agent-as-a-Service platform offering real-time AI voice agents for small businesses, supporting over 70 languages with low latency via model-agnostic routing and end-to-end audio processing.
details: Most small businesses still manage phone calls with human operators, menu trees, or voicemail, often failing to cover after-hours calls or multiple languages. This leads to dropped calls and repeated information for customers.

The goal was to create a real-time AI voice agent for phone calls, not a website chatbot, capable of operating in over 70 languages without needing a separate model for each. This led to the development of RingBot, an Agent-as-a-Service platform.

Traditional text-in-the-middle processing for voice adds 500ms-1s latency per step, making conversations feel robotic. Real-time voice models like GPT Realtime, Gemini Live, and Grok Voice use end-to-end audio pipelines, listening to and generating audio directly to cut latency dramatically.

RingBot is designed to be model-agnostic, routing calls to the most suitable real-time model based on the conversation's needs. This allows for flexibility and ensures the best possible experience, even allowing model switching mid-conversation.

Beyond just calling a model, RingBot's agent orchestrator manages intent classification, routing rules, tool calls (e.g., checking order status or booking appointments), and escalation thresholds to human agents.

A key finding was that multilingual voice is largely a solved problem at the model layer; the greater challenge lies in building the surrounding system. This includes managing fast-moving voice conversations and maintaining context.

To address this, RingBot maintains a structured conversation state that travels with the call. If a call is transferred, the human agent receives a short summary and the full transcript, eliminating the need for customers to repeat their story.

Despite the technical complexity, the end-user experience for small business owners is simplified through a straightforward configuration flow. Users connect business info, upload documents, pick a phone number, and deploy the agent.

This Agent-as-a-Service model means users "hire an agent" rather than dealing with a toolkit of telephony, embeddings, or model selection. RingBot aims to provide a complete solution for automated, multilingual customer service.
